about: The “Líbera nos” develops the final petition of the Lord's Prayer: “deliver us from evil”. It asks that deliverance through the intercession of the Virgin Mary, the Apostles Peter, Paul and Andrew, and all the saints. The priest says it secretly over the paten and signs himself with it, and only the closing Per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum is heard.

seg.nr: The priest takes the paten in his right hand, between the forefinger and the middle finger, holds it upright over the altar, and says the prayer silently.

seg.tr: Deliver us, we pray, Lord, from all evils, past, present, and future; and through the intercession of blessed and glorious Mary, ever Virgin and Mother of God, together with Your blessed Apostles Peter and Paul, Andrew, and all the saints,

fn.w001: A second-person singular imperative opening the prayer.
fn.w008: The first of three ablative plural adjectives agreeing with “malis” (w007).
fn.w013: A participle forming an ablative absolute with “Vírgine” (w018).
fn.w033: An adjective used as a noun: the holy ones.

seg.nr: The priest signs himself with the paten, from forehead to breast.

seg.tr: in Your kindness, grant peace in our days,

fn.w035: A nominative adjective agreeing with the understood subject of “da” (w034).

seg.tr: so that, upheld by Your mercy, we may always be free from sin and protected from every disturbance.

fn.w040: It introduces a purpose clause with “simus” (w048) as its verb.
fn.w044: A participle agreeing with the understood subject of “simus” (w048).
fn.w045: The first half of an et… et… pair with “et” (w051): both free from sin and safe from disquiet.
fn.w048: The verb of the clause introduced by “ut” (w040), with “líberi” (w050) and “secúri” (w055) as predicates.

seg.nr: The priest slips the paten under the Host, uncovers the chalice, genuflects, rises, takes the Host, and holding it over the chalice with both hands breaks it in two.

seg.tr: Through the same Jesus Christ, Your Son and our Lord,

seg.nr: The priest lays the half held in his right hand on the paten and breaks a small particle from the half remaining in his left.

seg.tr: who, being God, lives and reigns with You in the unity of the Holy Spirit,

fn.w065: The preposition “cum” is attached to the end of the pronoun “te”.
fn.w073: Nominative referring to the subject of “vivit” (w066) and “regnat” (w068).

seg.nr: The priest joins the other half to the half on the paten, holds the small particle over the chalice, and says in an audible voice or sings:
